title: Jump Game VI
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and an integer k, you start at index 0.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and an integer k, you start at index 0. In one move, you can jump to any index in the range from i + 1 to min(n - 1, i + k). The goal is to reach the last index of the array (index n - 1). Your score is the sum of nums[j] for each index j you visit during the process. Return the maximum score you can achieve by following these jumps.
constraints: Start at index zero and jump forward 1 through k positions until the final index.
Score includes every visited value; return the maximum possible score.
hints: The DP transition needs the largest score among the previous k indices.
Maintain those candidate scores in decreasing deque order.
Remove expired front indices, add nums[i] to the front score, pop dominated backs, and append i.
The deque front is always the maximum valid predecessor, and dominated smaller scores expire no later than the new score.
